content:
maria: Heads-up — after the driver v2.14 rollout I'm seeing a consistent p95 regression for long sequences (seqlen > 1024). Looks like the autotuner is flipping to a different kernel path and our KV cache behavior is getting worse at the same time.

maria: Repro steps I ran locally:
```
# synthetic load to reproduce tail latency
./perf_runner --model redwood-7b --seq-len 1200 --batch 1 --requests 5000
```

maria: Quick perf snippet from the run:
```
baseline: p95 ~ 240ms
after-driver: p95 ~ 275ms (+14%)
kernel_selector: many batches picked kernel_id=21 (matmul_fallback)
kvcache: miss rate spike ~30% coincident with kernel switch
```

sam: kernel_id=21 is the generic fallback path. For Ampere + seqlen>1024 we should prefer kernel_id=9 (packed_matmul). Did the cost table get rebuilt with incorrect costs?

nina: I ran the selector locally — the cost estimator returned higher exec time for kernel 9 because the seqlen distribution profile was stale (job used old profile). The autotune re-eval used that stale profile and favored 21.

alex: Is autotune persistence enabled? If persisted profiles were lost on the driver restart we might have cold autotune runs that pick suboptimal kernels until enough samples are gathered.

maria: Persistence is enabled but we expire profiles when driver hash changes. The driver bump changed the hash; the runtime reran autotune and tried to write new profiles. I see intermittent write errors in logs (permission denied).

devon: Do you have the exact write error? Could be a mount race during the rollout (remounted ro).

maria: log snippet: 
```
2024-06-14T16:13:22Z ERROR autotune: failed to persist profile model=redwood-7b driver_hash=0x7b3 err="permission denied"
```

ci-bot: @maria filed issue #4522 (eng-runtime) and attached logs and repro.

sam: Short-term mitigation idea: prevent aggressive KV eviction on kernel switch events if the upstream seqlen distribution hasn't materially changed. That avoids churn while autotune warms up. Longer term: make persistence atomic + retries and namespace profiles by (driver, runtime, model).

nina: Also propose salting profile keys with (driver_version, runtime_version, arch, seqlen_bin) and switch from immediate invalidation on minor driver bumps to TTL-based pruning and sample-count gating.

alex: +1. For rollouts we should hotswap autotune results only after the new profile has N successful samples. Two-phase swap.

devon: I'll open a small PR for the guarded fallback (skip eviction) and add a metric to detect kernel oscillation. Who owns persistence retry work?

maria: I'll take persistence retries + add a counter metric for persist failures. Devon owns the guarded fallback PR. Sam & Nina will review both.

sam: ack, will review today :thumbsup:

nina: add a histogram per seqlen-bin in the kernel selector (kernel_pick_by_seqlen_bin) so we can alert on sudden pick shifts.

maria: good call — I'll add a dashboard and an alert that fires on >10% shift in picks within 10m.

ci-bot: issue #4522 updated: labels=[bug, perf, autotune], assignees=[maria,devon]

alex: thanks folks. Target: guard+retry shipped by EOD tomorrow, instrumentation in next iteration.

maria: sounds good. I'll keep the issue updated with PR links and perf numbers.
